bmc-roadmachine-01: Compliant yet lively endurance bike with room for wide tires; very pricey, and a bit heavy for climbs.
bmc-roadmachine-x: Fast, sharp-handling all-road bike that suits pavement and light gravel; weak on rough gravel and mud.
bmc-teammachine-r-01: Fast and stiff on flat roads with sharp cornering; firmer over rough roads, and crosswinds can push it.
bmc-teammachine-slr: Comfortable yet snappy, stiff and efficient, and owners love it; stock wheels are basic.
bmc-teammachine-slr-01: Stiff, fast and sharp in corners; many find the ride firm and the tires narrow for the price.
bmc-urs: Slack, mountain-bike-style geometry that riders love on rough gravel; a few say cheaper bikes match it.
bmc-urs-01: Rear damper and wide tires smooth rough gravel and washboard; the stock gearing spins out.
bmc-urs-al: Planted gravel handling with big tire clearance for the money; the long reach needs a short stem.
cannondale-caad14: Sharp, lively race handling in a stiff alloy frame; many find the full builds poor value.
cannondale-jekyll: Composed, grippy and fast on rough, steep descents; heavy to climb, and the shock is fiddly to reach.
cannondale-scalpel: Fast, efficient climber with sharp handling and a calm 120 mm rear end; dropper and gearing gripes.
cannondale-scalpel-ht: Very light, fast climber that rides comfortably for a hardtail; skittish and harsh on rough descents.
cannondale-superx: Fast, lively and road-like on gravel with sharp handling; firm on stock tires, so wider rubber helps.
cannondale-trail: Tough, capable hardtail for beginners and easy trails; basic parts show on rougher ground.
canyon-aeroad-cfr: Stiff, fast and stable at speed with adjustable bars; the low, racy fit and fixed parts annoy some.
canyon-lux-trail-cf: Light and efficient on climbs yet confident on rough descents; some find it heavy with weak brakes.
canyon-spectral-cf: Playful, balanced all-rounder that climbs better than expected; the steering damper and reach irk some.
cervelo-s5: Very fast and steady in crosswinds with a calm ride; toe overlap and a firm back end annoy a few.
cervelo-soloist: Sharp, stable handling and good value for a race bike; heavy stock wheels and wide bars invite swaps.
giant-contend-ar: Comfortable, versatile aluminium all-road bike with generous tire room; a proprietary seatpost irks some.
giant-reign-advanced-pro: Lively, composed enduro bike that climbs better than expected; a few want stronger brakes and storage.
giant-stance: Great-value starter full-suspension that climbs well; budget brakes and narrow bars often need upgrading.
giant-tcr-advanced-pro: Light, snappy and sharp in corners with good-value spec; hookless wheels limit tire choice for some.
pivot-firebird: Balanced enduro bike with firm, bob-free climbing; pricey, and the stiff frame can feel harsh.
pivot-shadowcat: Playful, lively 27.5 inch trail bike that climbs well; the small wheels roll less smoothly over chunk.
pivot-switchblade: Agile, poppy and capable on climbs and descents; expensive, and the wide hub spacing limits wheel swaps.
pivot-trailcat-lt: Climbs well and stays playful and composed downhill; very pricey, with grabby brakes and tiny storage.
pivot-trailcat-sl: Pedals up fast and tracks rough ground well for 120 mm; a bit heavy, and the seat pitches riders back.
santa-cruz-5010: Playful, precise handling that pops off everything; the weak stock brakes and high price draw complaints.
santa-cruz-bronson: Planted and composed on steep, rough trails yet still climbs well; some note chain slap and a stiff feel.
santa-cruz-hightower: Confident on steep descents yet climbs without bob; many call it pricey, with no cheaper alloy option.
santa-cruz-megatower: Stable and composed when charged hard through rough terrain; heavy, with a stiff feel at slow speeds.
santa-cruz-tallboy: Composed in rough terrain and lively on trails, with calm climbing; pricey, and some get pedal strikes.
santa-cruz-v10: Huge grip and composed speed on steep, rough tracks with plenty of fit tweaks; fork setup takes patience.
specialized-aethos-2: Light, compliant and comfortable on long hilly rides; the stock tires and wheels invite upgrades.
specialized-chisel: Light, efficient climber and good value for full-suspension XC; heavy stock parts, shaky on drops.
specialized-rockhopper: Dependable starter hardtail with simple one-by shifting; the basic fork and hubs limit upgrades.
specialized-s-works-epic-9: Very light, fast XC racer that still descends well; the very high price and headset routing irk.
specialized-stumpjumper-15: Versatile, tunable trail bike with a plush shock that climbs well; a few find it loses support in chunk.
trek-check-out-sl: Smooths rough gravel and washboard with short-travel suspension; heavy, and overkill on smooth ground.
trek-fuel-ex-gen-7: Versatile, confident all-rounder that climbs comfortably; the alloy builds are heavy.
yeti-asr: Smooth, calm and grippy for a lightweight XC bike; alloy wheels on a pricey build draw complaints.
yeti-sb115: Excellent technical climber with lively, precise handling; gets nervous when speed and chunk rise.
yeti-sb120: Climbs well and descends as if it had more travel; on the heavy side, with no storage and a steep front.
yeti-sb135: Nimble, playful 27.5 inch ride that rails corners and climbs well; blunter in chunk and pricey.
